question: Which ancient Indian sport pits crowds of brave young men against angry bulls?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jallikattu is a traditional event celebrated in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

 
 
• In Jallikattu the bull (Kangayam breed) is released into a crowd of people and many human participants try to catch the large hump on the bull's back.
 
• It is celebrated on Mattu Pongal day as a part of Pongal celebrations.
 
• Alanganallur is a panchayat town in the Madurai district of Tamil Nadu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kho** **Kho** **-**

 
 
• **Kho Kho** is a** traditional Indian sport **that has existed in some form or the other for **thousands of years**.
 
• A competitive** Kho Kho playing field **is rectangular in shape,** measuring 27mx16m**.
 
• The **two 27m lines** are called sidelines while the **two 16m lines **are the end lines.
 
 
 
• **Kabaddi - **
 
 
• It is a team sport.
 
• It consists of 2 teams of 7 players each facing the other.
 
• It is an Indian game but is now played worldwide.
 
• It consists of a raider team and an anti-raider team.​
 
 
 
• Mallakhamb - 
 
 
• Mallakhamb is a traditional sport, originating from the Indian subcontinent, in which a gymnast performs aerial yoga or gymnastic postures and wrestling grips in concert with vertical stationery or a hanging wooden pole, cane, or rope.
 
• The word Mallakhamb also refers to the pole used in the sport.
 
• On April 9, 2013, the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh declared Mallakhamba the state sport.
 
• Madhya Pradesh, also known as the “Heart of India”, has been home to the cultural and spiritual heritage of almost all religions.
 
• Innumerable monuments, intricately carved temples, stupas, forts and palaces are dotted all over the State.
